Lets face it architecture and interior design have become a bit lazy these days. Theyve become a series of rectangles and right angles that are connected to the next space that looks and feels like everything else youve ever experienced. Very little is left to the imagination. And yet, if youre lucky enough to find one, the best designed spaces have a capacity to make you feel something - something fresh, or even invigorating. Such the case with Residence #3430 in the Four Seasons Private Residences building. What started out as a pretty standard floor plan quickly became something significantly better and more meaningful once the current owners took roughly 500 square feet from the home next door, which they also owned. This expansion was the genesis for what has become a wholly unique property inside the Four Seasons. The owners' goal was simple: to design a space in which form and function have equal standing, while also making it stylish - even a bit sexy. Graceful curves replaced hard right angles, creating an almost organic flow throughout. Curvilinear walls and ceilings add a touch of intrigue, while actually increasing functionality. This is where you come when you want to create a life that serves you; where time becomes your ally, and not your foe; where HOW you spend your time is dictated by what you determine your priorities to be.
